body:
Manual GUI test passed on 2026-11-20.

On `O4 Cam Plate master`, I selected several edges for 2D Chamfer and generated the operation. The viewport showed the expected toolpath on the selected edges. The test did not require a closed loop.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4e22c8dbe915bfa9131486395c4237898532370d -->
Review at head 4e22c8dbe. Read, not built: the PR is from a fork, so its code does not run on the maintainer's runners, and no local build slot was free.

The change reads well:
- `chamfer_open_runs` validates the parameters first, refuses an empty selection, a non-finite corner depth, a chain with no model wall at the programmed depth, and a collapsed segment. Each refusal says what to do. The material side comes from a model read at the two chamfer heights, so climb does not depend on the stored edge direction. Provenance is in the file header.
- The selection wiring adds `Chamfer2D` beside Contour and PlasmaProfile for open runs (#670 pattern). No new command, so no MCP tool is owed.
- The pinning tests cover one edge, connected edges as one run, separate chains as separate passes, and no credit for an unselected edge. File sizes obey the 400-line rule. `docs/decisions/2988-chamfer-open-edge-chains.md` is in the PR. No snapshot PNG is touched.
- The red heavy step you report is not yours: on a platform outside the three pins, `bore_path_matches` still uses the pre-solidcore fallback band, so the same step is red on plain main. I filed #3085 for it.

One requested change:
- The three new refusal branches have no pinning test. Add a test for each: a run with a collapsed segment, an open edge with no model wall at the chamfer depth, and picks that are open runs under Boundary settings that shape an area. Assert the refusal and the message name. This is safety-floor code, so each refusal needs its proof.

Labels are not changed by this review.
Review fix in progress. I will add tests for all three open-chain refusal branches and rerun the focused gate.

Addressed the review at `2fbe6f2fb`.

I added three focused tests. They cover a collapsed segment, no model wall at the chamfer depth, and open runs with area-shaping Boundary settings. The first two now reach explicit chamfer refusal branches. The Boundary refusal now runs before the generic unsupported-area result.

Results:
- Motion tests: 12 passed.
- App tests: 5 passed.
- Clippy: passed.
- Quick gate: 236 of 236 steps passed.
- Heavy gate: 235 of 236 steps passed. The same unrelated `pocket3d_hsm` failure reproduces on unchanged `origin/main` and is tracked in #3085.

The PR is ready for a second review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 2fbe6f2fbb33d3be8181ae6097766f2b1415c94e -->
Review at head 2fbe6f2fb. Read, not built: the PR is from a fork, so its code does not run on the maintainer's runners, and no local build slot was free. The only commit since the reviewed head 4e22c8dbe is 2fbe6f2fb, and it answers the one requested change:

- Collapsed segment: `chamfer_open_runs` now checks every segment pair before use, with a finite and 1e-9 length test, and the refusal names the remedy (re-pick the edge). Pinned by `an_open_chamfer_with_a_collapsed_segment_refuses_by_name`.
- No model wall: pinned by `an_open_chamfer_without_a_model_wall_refuses_by_name` (the refusal text predates this commit; the proof did not).
- Open runs under Boundary settings that shape an area: the refusal moved from the contour arm to the top of `run_job_arms`, where it gates before the arm consumes the selection - that was the door that did not open. Pinned by `open_chamfer_runs_with_boundary_area_settings_refuse_by_name`.

I traced the moved check: it fires only for Chamfer2D with a selection whose picks are open runs with no loops, and the earlier `.take()` paths belong to other kinds, so `contour_sel` is still present at the gate. The refusal message is unchanged. File sizes obey the rule for the touched code; `generate.rs` is pre-existing over 400 lines and this commit adds 12.

Clean. One gap for the record: the push carries no gate report for the quick gate at 2fbe6f2fb. Please post the quick-gate result for this head (or state it in the body) - the change is safety-floor code, and the merge batch reads it.

Labels: merge-ready set; the merge decision for this floor work rides with the maintainer's second read.
